reader.requirement: At --std 85, outside the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph HIGH-VALUE is the character at the highest position of the program collating sequence (native highest with no PCS or an identity alphabet; for a literal-phrase alphabet the largest unspecified native character; only when every character is specified, the specified highest position, a tie there going to the last character specified), in every use (VALUE, MOVE, group fill, relation and condition-name tests, INSPECT, STRING) and in contained programs.

reader.notes: CollatingTable.Build computes HIGH-VALUE once per alphabet (Extremes): the largest native code unit the definition leaves unspecified, else the tie rule over the specified positions taking the last specified; FillChar and LiteralEnvironment read it for every alphanumeric use outside SPECIAL-NAMES. The refusal half and the file/size classes do not reach this general rule.

refuter.evidence: r3rev-001: PCS ALPHABET AL IS 65536 THRU 1 (every native character specified, descending): VALUE HIGH-VALUE = U+0000 (HV-00), MOVE HIGH-VALUES fills U+0000 (MV-HV-00), LOW-VALUE = U+FFFF (LV-FF), "A" > "B" under the PCS. r3top-002: every character specified with a three-way ALSO tie at the highest position, 65536 ALSO 65534 ALSO 66 last: HIGH-VALUE is the last specified, A (HV=A, MV=AA). r5sn-002: PCS LOW-VALUES THRU "@" "Q" HIGH-VALUES: procedure HIGH-VALUE is U+FFFE, the largest unspecified (U+FFFF is specified).
